title_original: MBZUAI Announces International Open call for Public Artwork

blocks.text: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) has announced an international commission for a new public artwork at its Abu Dhabi campus, inviting artists and collectives to submit proposals for a sculpture or installation. The selected work will become part of the university’s permanent art collection and be displayed in an indoor atrium at its forthcoming cultural centre, set to open in 2027.

With a budget of up to USD 250,000, the commission invites artists to focus on the intersections of art, science and technology, drawing on one or more of three proposed areas of inquiry. These include the UAE’s landscape, heritage and communities; artificial intelligence and scientific research; and the historical development of science and computation, particularly the connections between art, mathematics and machines.

Proposals will be reviewed and assessed by a panel comprising MBZUAI Vice President and Chief of Staff Dekyi (Hong) Liang; Head of Art, Archives and Special Collections Jasmine Soliman; Campus Development and Architecture Project Manager Dominic Xie and Dyala Nusseibeh , Director of Frieze Abu Dhabi.

Dekyi (Hong) Liang noted: “MBZUAI was founded to push the frontiers of research in artificial intelligence and the broader science and technology disciplines. It is also our responsibility to invest in cultivating a culture that embraces creativity and innovation. Art has always been part of that story of human endeavour. This commission reflects our commitment to creating a campus where science and culture converge, and where students, researchers and visitors experience tangible ambition, something that inspires our community to aim higher.”

The commission also reflects MBZUAI’s ambition to expand its cultural and academic remit beyond artificial intelligence and computer science. As Jasmine Soliman, Head of Art, Archives and Special Collections at MBZUAI, noted: “We shaped this open call as an extension of the collection we have built, which holds works spanning a century by artists who engage science through research, method and technique, treating knowledge as both an intellectual tradition and a material practice. The commission will join that collection as a site-specific work within the forthcoming cultural centre, a place for exhibition, performance and public programs, as MBZUAI broadens into a comprehensive university, with the humanities and social sciences among its academic divisions.”
